Multi-omics survival analysis

Source: vignettes/multi-omic-analysis.Rmd
multi-omic-analysis.Rmd
library(Omics2Surv)

Introduction

This vignette walks through a complete multi-omics survival analysis workflow, from data acquisition to patient stratification and functional enrichment. As a working example we use the TCGA-KIPAN cohort (kidney pan-cancer), retrieving RNA-seq, copy number variation (CNV) and DNA methylation data together with the corresponding clinical information.

While three omics layers are downloaded and assembled into a single MultiAssayExperiment (MAE), this vignette focuses on combining multiple omics (RNA-seq and Methylation), using early, late, and joint integration strategies. For a workflow that models each omic independently, see the companion vignette("single-omic-analysis").

Data acquisition & exploration

We start by retrieving the omics and clinical data from LinkedOmics for the TCGA-KIPAN cohort.

KIPANRNA_link = retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN","RNAseq (HiSeq, Gene level)")

KIPANCN_link = retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "SCNV (Gene level, Thresholded)")

KIPAN_Meth_link= retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "Methylation (Gene level, HM450K)")

KIPANClin_link= retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "Clinical")

Exploration

Before any modeling step, it is good practice to explore the data structure. explore_pca() performs a principal component analysis on the RNA-seq data and relates the resulting components to a set of clinical/metadata variables.

data_expl= explore_pca(KIPANRNA_link, KIPANClin_link, metavars = c("histological_type", "gender", "radiation_therapy", "race", "ethnicity"))

data_expl$eigencorplot

Data preselection

Optional splitting

The cohort is split into a training and a test set. The same split is shared across all omics layers so that the same patients end up in the training set (and the same patients in the test set) for every modality.

KIPAN_split <- split_train_test(
  omics_list     = list(mRNA = KIPANRNA_link,
                        CNV  = KIPANCN_link, methyl = KIPAN_Meth_link),
  clinical_data  = KIPANClin_link
)

Variable screening

Each omic is preprocessed and screened on the training set only, to avoid information leakage from the test set. Here RNA-seq features are selected in an unsupervised fashion based on highly variable genes, CNV features are selected based on sparsity, and methylation features are selected based on interquartile range (IQR).

KIPAN_RNA_train=prepare_RNA(KIPAN_split$train_list$mRNA,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical,method = "unsupervised", unsupervised_method= "A", hvg_threshold = 5)
KIPAN_CNV_train=prepare_CNV(KIPAN_split$train_list$CNV,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical,method = "unsupervised", unsupervised_method = "sparsity", top_n_features = 800)
KIPAN_Meth_train=prepare_methyl(KIPAN_split$train_list$methyl,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical, method="unsupervised", unsupervised_method = "IQR", hvg_threshold = 5)

The same features selected on the training set are then applied to the test set with prepare_test_SE(), so that train and test share an identical feature space.

KIPAN_RNA_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$mRNA,   KIPAN_RNA_train)
KIPAN_Meth_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$methyl,  KIPAN_Meth_train)
KIPAN_CNV_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$CNV,   KIPAN_CNV_train)
omics_train = list(mRNA=KIPAN_RNA_train, CNV=KIPAN_CNV_train, meth= KIPAN_Meth_train)

omics_test = list(mRNA= KIPAN_RNA_test, CNV= KIPAN_CNV_test, meth= KIPAN_Meth_test)

MAE building with 3 omics

The preprocessed omics and the clinical data are assembled into a MultiAssayExperiment object, separately for the training and the test set.

KIPAN_MAE_train = build_MAE(omics_list = omics_train, KIPAN_split$train_clinical)

KIPAN_MAE_test=build_MAE(omics_list = omics_test, KIPAN_split$test_clinical)

Multi-omics modeling: RNA + Methylation

From this point on we focus on combining the RNA-seq and methylation layers (omic_list = c("mRNA", "meth")) using several integration strategies.

Penalized regression - Early integration

In early integration, the features from the different omics are concatenated before fitting a single penalized regression model.

#lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_lasso",
  nfolds = 10,
  nlambda = 200
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_lasso"
)
#adaptive lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso",
  nfolds = 10,
  nlambda = 200
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso"
)
#elastic net
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net",
  nfolds= 10,
  nlambda = 200
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net"
)
#aft pen
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "aft_pen",
  nfolds = 10,
  nlambda= 200
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "early",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

Penalized regression - Late integration

In late integration, a separate model is fitted on each omic and the resulting predictions are then combined. We used the Robust Rank Aggregation method.

#lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_lasso"
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_lasso"
)
#adaptive lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso"
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso"
)
#elastic net
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net"
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net"
)
#aft pen
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  integration  = "late",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

Joint integration

Joint integration methods model all omics simultaneously within a single algorithm. Here we use cooperative regularized Cox regression (CoopCox), a random-forest based approach for blockwise data (blockForest), and a cooperative AFT model (AFTCoop).

KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_j_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "CoopCox",
  folds = 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_j_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "CoopCox"
)
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_j_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "blockForest",
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_j_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "blockForest"
)
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_j_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "AFTCoop"
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_j_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  joint_method = "AFTCoop"
)

Flexynesis

Finally, we train a deep-learning based multi-omics model using Flexynesis. Flexynesis is a Python package, so before running the chunks below you need to set up a dedicated Python environment with Python >= 3.11 and install Flexynesis in it:

# requires mamba (https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation.html)
mamba create --name flexynesisenv python==3.11
mamba activate flexynesisenv

# install the latest version from PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/flexynesis)
python -m pip install flexynesis --upgrade
KIPAN_MAE_train <- train_flexynesis_models(
  mae_train  = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list  = c("mRNA", "meth"),
  threads= 19 #change this to the number of threads available on your machine
)

KIPAN_MAE_test <- predict_flexynesis_models(
  mae_pred   = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train  = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list  = c("mRNA", "meth")
)

C-index tables

benchmark_models() collects the concordance index (C-index) achieved by every model trained so far and returns a comparison table. Here we restrict the comparison to the early, late, joint, and Flexynesis.

KIPAN_table= benchmark_models(KIPAN_MAE_train, KIPAN_MAE_test,
                 keep_integrations = c("early", "late", "joint", "flexynesis"))

Patient stratification

Using the risk scores from the best performing multi-omics model (blockForest in this example), patients can be stratified into risk groups and the results visualized with Kaplan-Meier curves, UMAP embeddings, and heatmaps.

KIPAN_multi_strat <- patient_stratification(KIPAN_MAE_train, KIPAN_MAE_test,
                                            model = "blockForest",
                                            method = "survcutpoint",
                                            plot_scores = TRUE)
plot_km(KIPAN_multi_strat)
plot_umap(KIPAN_MAE_test, KIPAN_multi_strat, model = "blockForest", mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train, top_feat = 100)
plot_heatmap(KIPAN_MAE_test, KIPAN_multi_strat, model = "blockForest",
             top_feat = 50, mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train)

Finally, the user defined top features by model importance can be tested for functional enrichment.

KIPAN_block <- enrich_features(KIPAN_MAE_train, model = "blockForest",
                                  top_feat = 50,
                                  strip_prefix = "^(mRNA|meth)_",
                               pvalue_cutoff = 0.07,
  qvalue_cutoff = 0.2)
plot_enrichment(KIPAN_block, "GO")
